data.eligibility_information:
• MSc or PhD (completed or in progress) in biological sciences, biochemistry, molecular biology, or related life sciences discipline. Or: MBBS, nursing, or a health sciences background. 
• Strong communication in Hindi and English. 
• Based in Bengaluru. This is not a remote role.
data.additional_information:
We’re hiring a Program Executive for a new program we are launching in our hospitals - someone who will work closely alongside a small group of cancer patients and their families through their treatment journey. Your job is to be the person they turn for everything that isn’t a clinical decision. 

Think of it this way: the oncologist decides the treatment. You help the patient and their family navigate everything around it. 

This is a pilot program. You won’t be following a manual; you’ll be helping us write one. The role will evolve based on what patients actually need, and you’ll shape that directly. 

The work is patient-facing, in-person, and deeply human. Some days will be logistics. Some days will be sitting with someone who’s frightened. Some days will be both.
data.additional_details:
What’s In It For You 
If you’re studying biological sciences, especially in areas adjacent to oncology — this program gives you something a lab can’t. 

Shape how cancer patients are treated, not just in theory. 
You’ll be part of building structured treatment plans for real patients. If your academic work touches molecular testing, tumour biology, or drug mechanisms, this is where you see those concepts land in a patient’s life. You’ll speak to patients directly, help them understand their treatment, and see how clinical decisions play out in practice. That’s a perspective most researchers never get. 

Build real-world evidence for your academic work. 
You’ll be running a program from the ground up - working with patients whose treatment may be (or may not be) informed by molecular testing, organ-specific protocols, or newer drug regimens. You’ll see outcomes firsthand. Whether you’re writing a thesis or building a research career, having designed and executed a patient-facing program in oncology care is a powerful addition.  

Be the bridge between medicine and the people it’s meant to serve. 
Cancer patients and their caregivers are overwhelmed, under-informed, and often alone. The doctor has 10 minutes. The family has a hundred questions. You’ll be the person who closes that gap - translating, guiding, and being present when it matters most. If you got into biology because you cared about human health, this is the most direct version of that. 

What We’re Looking For 
We’re not hiring for just expertise. We’re hiring for how you think, how you learn, and how you show up for people. 

A learning mindset. 
Every piece of information in this program is captured in systems you’ll need to learn quickly. New tools, new terminology, new workflows - every week. We need someone who’s genuinely curious, who asks questions before they assume, and who treats not knowing something as a starting point, not a problem. 

Empathy. 
You’ll speak to patients and caregivers who are going through the hardest time of their lives. This isn’t just about saying the right words - it’s about listening, being present, and making people feel like they’re not alone. If you’re the kind of person others naturally open to, that matters more than your GPA here. 

Attention to detail. 
This is a 0-to-1 role, and you’re working with real patients. Every person you support has a specific history, specific fears, and specific needs. You must remember (or build a system to capture) that Mrs. Sharma is anxious about her next scan, that Ravi’s caregiver needs the appointment moved to Tuesday, that someone’s diet can't be solid food led. These are real people. Details matter because people matter. 

Willingness to try new tools. 
We use technology to track, coordinate, and communicate. You don’t need to be technical, but you need to be comfortable picking up new software, learning a CRM, using shared dashboards, and figuring things out without a training manual. 

Systems thinking. 
You won’t just execute a program - you’ll co-create it with us. That means seeing patterns across patients, identifying what’s working and what’s breaking, and thinking about how individual interactions connect to a larger system. We need someone who can zoom out from “this patient needs X” to “our process should handle X better” 

What This Isn’t 
This is not a clinical role. You will not diagnose, prescribe, or make treatment decisions. You will not replace the oncologist, the nurse, or the therapist. 
You’re being hired because cancer patients need someone in their corner who can help them make sense of a confusing, frightening experience - and right now, nobody does that job.

questions.question: Share a short note (not a cover letter) on why this interests you
Tell us about a time you helped someone through something difficult - a health scare, a confusing process, a hard decision. What did you do, and what did you learn about yourself?
